description: Computer Science senior and volunteer forest firefighter combining field experience with Python and Digital Image Processing. Developing 'AeroGuard' to harmonize MODIS and VIIRS data for real-time wildfire and smoke detection. Not looking for additional members as I am tackling this challenge solo to apply my academic research directly to Earth observation solutions.
summary: Satellite active-fire records from NASA FIRMS are split across sensors with incompatible spatial physics: MODIS nadir pixels cover 1 km² (expanding to >10 km² at scan edges due to bow-tie distortion), whereas VIIRS S-NPP and NOAA-20 cover 0.14 km² (375 m), detecting smaller and cooler fires. Summing raw detections creates an artificial 4.43x jump in 2012 and a 1.72x raw-sum jump in 2018, misleading multi-decade trend analyses and operational triage. AeroGuard solves this with a two-stage harmonization engine and a 6-tab bilingual (EN/PT) web platform covering 17 years (2010–2026; 3.55 million detections) across Minas Gerais and the Brazilian Cerrado transition (~1.26M km²). First, near-real-time detections are physically normalized by actual pixel footprint area (scan x track) into Fire Radiative Power area-density (MW/km²) on a 0.02° grid with 2D spatial filtering. Second, VIIRS records (2012–2026) are calibrated to a homogeneous MODIS baseline using overlap-period scaling, removing the 2012 step artifact (0.93x vs. 0.93x control; 3.5% Leave-One-Year-Out median bias) and translating one harmonized dataset into actionable views for Firefighters, Land Managers, and Scientists. The 17-year record also isolates 276 Priority Zones (fire in at least 90% of years) for firebreak planning and brigade pre-positioning.
details:
What It Does & Why It Matters

AeroGuard bridges the gap between raw orbital thermal anomalies and real-world wildfire decision-making. In raw NASA FIRMS data, sensor transitions (MODIS to VIIRS S-NPP in 2012 and NOAA-20 in 2018) and off-nadir bow-tie pixel growth distort both spatial triage and historical fire calendars. AeroGuard harmonizes 17 years of MODIS and VIIRS active-fire records (2010–2026) and delivers a live, bilingual (EN/PT) web platform for three audiences:

- Combat (Firefighters): reduces 42,616 near-real-time detections to 14,965 harmonized grid cells (64.9% less spatial redundancy), highlights 1,091 fire fronts confirmed by both MODIS and VIIRS, and flags large off-nadir edge pixels (>3 km²) that need field verification.

- Prevention (Land Managers): condenses 17 complete years of fire history into 276 strict Priority Zones (cells with fire in at least 90% of years AND in the top 10% of active fire days per year). Pre-season firebreaks and brigade positioning can focus on about 2.6% of the study area (~32,830 km²), including a cell on the Ouro Branco / Congonhas axis, MG (-20.55, -43.95), with fire in 17 of 17 years.

- Science (Researchers): co-located sensor pairing, separable 2D image-processing kernels, Leave-One-Year-Out (LOYO) validation metrics, and a 2010–2026 burning calendar with P10–P90 climatological bands.

How It Works (Two-Stage Harmonization)

1. Physical footprint and FRP-density harmonization (src/harmonize.py)

- Computes the true ground footprint of each detection: A_pixel = scan x track (km²).

- Aggregates detections into Fire Radiative Power (FRP) area-density (MW/km²) on a configurable 0.02° grid (~4.8 km²).

- Applies separable 2D kernels (Gaussian, Box, Laplacian-of-Gaussian) to delineate fire fronts and suppress isolated noise.

- Uses n = 296 near-simultaneous MODIS/VIIRS pairs (|Δt| <= 90 min). The VIIRS/MODIS density ratio increases with MODIS pixel size (Spearman r = +0.59, p < 0.0001), consistent with the geometric explanation.

2. 17-year cross-era calibration (src/climatology.py)

- Consolidates 3.55 million detections (621,158 cell-days, 2010–2026) into a Parquet archive.

- Aligns VIIRS S-NPP and NOAA-20 to the homogeneous MODIS baseline using the median ratio over overlap years (k_SNPP = 0.377, k_NOAA20 = 0.371).

- Leave-One-Year-Out cross-validation over 15 overlap years gives a median annual bias of 3.5% (S-NPP) and 4.5% (NOAA-20). The artificial 4.43x jump in 2012 drops to 0.93x, matching the 0.93x MODIS-only control. (The 2018 drop is real: the MODIS-only control also falls to 0.45x, and AeroGuard tracks it at 0.54x.)

Data, Tools and AI Use

- Data: NASA FIRMS active-fire products (MODIS MCD14DL, VIIRS S-NPP VNP14IMGTDL, VIIRS NOAA-20 VJ114IMGTDL), 2010–2026, Minas Gerais and Cerrado transition (~1.26M km²).

- Languages and libraries: Python 3, Streamlit, Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, Requests, PyArrow (Parquet), LaTeX (Beamer).

- AI use: AI assistants helped with code refactoring, bilingual localization and slide structuring. All harmonization equations, statistics and priority zones are 100% deterministic (Python/NumPy/Pandas). An optional LLM text rewrite (NVIDIA NIM llama-3.1-8b) is rejected by our numbers_ok() validator if it contains any number outside the audited JSON.

- Live app: https://aeroguard-spaceapps.streamlit.app

- Code: https://github.com/Alefe-Tonidandel/SpaceApps2026-AeroGuard
